observations:
Torah LM2 #125 is an extremely brief teaching — a reported conversation between Rebbe Nachman and one of his students about the practice of saying Tehillim. The entire text is seven lines long.

The text contains only ONE explicit bechina equation: 'בִּבְחִינַת הַנְּקֻדָּה טוֹבָה הַזֹּאת הוּא בְּחִינַת חָסִיד' — the nekuda tova (good point) and being a chasid are explicitly equated as two expressions of the same essential quality. This single bechina pair is too small to constitute a package on its own (a package requires a connected cluster, not an isolated pair).

The remaining conceptual vocabulary of the teaching (saying Tehillim, war against the yetzer hara, judging oneself favorably, morning prayers, Yehoshafat's elevated heart) is expressed through narrative and prescriptive language — eitza flows — not through bechina equations. These concepts describe the practice and its consequences, not parallel-nature relationships.

For a new package to be warranted, the spec requires 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. This Torah provides only 2 explicitly bechina-linked concepts (נקודה טובה and חסיד). The threshold for a new package is not met.

Recommendation: When this Torah is encoded into the dataset, the single bechina pair (נקודה טובה — חסיד) should be entered as one edge. Given the broader context of the teaching, these two nodes would form a minimal 2-node package under the domain of positive spiritual self-identity (good polarity). The teaching should cross-reference LM1 Torah 282 ('אֲזַמְּרָה לֵאלֹקַי בְּעוֹדִי') and LM2 Torah 101, which are explicitly cited in the text as parallel treatments of the same theme.
